newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices ease on low mill demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices ease on low mill demand.

text.p: Indian cotton prices eased on Wednesday on low mill demand and higher new crop arrivals, dealers said.

Volumes however were low as major players kept away awaiting the outcome of the meeting of Cotton Advisory Board convened on Thursday by the Textile Commissioner. The board normally discusses production and targets.

In spot deals Bengal Desi slid by 5/10 rupees at 875/900 rupees per maund (37.32 Kg) while Punjab saw ginned fell by 10 to 1530/1640 rupees. Gujarat Sankar 4 (long staple) fell by 200 to 18,000/18,800 rupees per candy (355.56Kg).
